benchmark_scope.description: Bounded 27-reference sample of prominent vehicle corridors and workbook-named road facilities spanning California, Arizona, New Mexico and Texas. It is not an exhaustive inventory or a measured traffic ranking.
benchmark_scope.selection: Four California gateways; six Arizona vehicle facilities; two New Mexico vehicle corridors; fifteen selected Texas bridges.
benchmark_scope.road_policy: motorway/trunk/primary including links; no automatic addition of secondary/local roads. Only separately reviewed explicit source-supported or workbook-named exceptions may be admitted.
benchmark_scope.membership_status: These are named road references to test against main-road candidates. Being in this sample does not assert any OSM road class or automatically admit a small road.
benchmark_scope.denominator_limit: Full-frontier recall cannot be calculated from a selected sample; candidate contacts, named facilities and individual directional gates have different units.

sources.title: TxDOT Border Crossings GIS
claims: Named facility points across the Texas–Mexico frontier; facility names and vehicle-mode attributes.
limits: Service description says valid as of 2021; layer edit timestamp is not a per-facility observation date.
Source has 28 rows including dams and a ferry; it is not a verified current open-crossing list.
Facility points need not lie exactly on the border or on a specific lane.
Falcon Dam coordinate appears in the Amistad area and is withheld from matching.

sources.title: Land Ports of Entry, Technical Freight Projects Integration Viewer
claims: California named POE locations, route-number field, and existing/future classification.
limits: Includes proposed Otay Mesa East and pedestrian CBX, which are not included in road benchmark.
Point geometry is a reference position, not a surveyed frontier contact.
Date fields are metadata edits, not observations of operational status.

sources.title: Ports of Entry CA Mexico
sources.publisher: San Diego Association of Governments; California Border Patrol; San Diego County OES
claims: Six named California facility points allow comparison of published reference positions.
limits: Upstream independence from Caltrans/OSM and per-point survey dates are undocumented.
Andrade point differs from Caltrans by roughly 13 km; Calexico West differs by roughly 850 m. These are unresolved source-coordinate discrepancies.

sources.title: Border Wait Times XML feed
claims: Named road and pedestrian reporting facilities, distinct cargo/passenger reporting units, and duplicate/umbrella feed records.
limits: 55 Mexican-border reporting records are not 55 distinct physical crossings.
Operational statuses in a morning live feed can mean routine hours/lane updates; they are not historical closure evidence.
No coordinates provided in this feed.

sources.title: Border Crossing/Entry Data FAQ
claims: Statistical ports aggregate individual bridges and transport infrastructure; Laredo is an explicit example.
Counts are inbound movements, not unique people/vehicles or outbound totals.

sources.title: ADOT MPO/COG Manual, Table 15-3
claims: Table names San Luis I/II, Lukeville, Sasabe, Mariposa and DeConcini and their access-road references and transport modes.
sources.access: Substantive indexed table text; full PDF download returned 403 and browser file was too large
limits: Historical table; traffic counts and opening hours not promoted to current assertions.
Route references identify approach corridors, not OSM classifications.

sources.title: Analysis of Bluetooth and Wi-Fi Technology to Measure Wait Times of Personal Vehicles at Arizona-Mexico Ports of Entry
claims: Mariposa links Nogales, Arizona/Sonora via SR 189 and Mexican Federal Highway 15D.

sources.title: Priority LPOE Projects
claims: Distinguishes existing Raul Hector Castro facility from proposed West Douglas commercial project; identifies Arizona POEs and pedestrian Morley Gate.
limits: Photographs generally circa 2013; page refers to 2022 funding.

sources.title: Dennis DeConcini Land Port of Entry
claims: Facility at 9 N Grand Ave, downtown Nogales; Morley Gate is pedestrian component, separate from vehicle lanes.

sources.title: NM 136 Interchange Feasibility Study
claims: NM 136 milepost 0 is Santa Teresa POE; four-lane major arterial connecting port to I-10 via Artcraft Road.
sources.access: Substantive indexed primary-page text; direct web open returned 403

sources.title: Columbus
claims: Columbus–Palomas facility serves vehicle, commercial and pedestrian traffic; distinct livestock crossing facility is not interchangeable with road gates.
limits: Undated page retains prospective 2015 construction text, so operational hours not treated as current.

sources.title: NM 11 Corridor Study
sources.publisher: New Mexico Department of Transportation / Southwest New Mexico Council of Governments
claims: NM 11 links Columbus LPOE to Deming and I-10.

sources.title: CSMS 58577932: Temporary Suspension of Operations at Lukeville
claims: Names Lukeville and both vehicle/pedestrian directions for historical suspension; establishes workbook crossing identity only for this geography benchmark.

sources.title: Texas-Mexico Border Transportation Master Plan update
claims: Separates vehicle, rail and pedestrian facilities; source GIS list is not an exhaustive all-mode frontier truth set.

sources.title: Arizona Buildings and Facilities
claims: San Luis I is at State Highway 95 and the international boundary; San Luis II is at 1375 South Avenue East.
Raul Hector Castro facility in Douglas is on Pan American Avenue; DeConcini is on North Grand Avenue.
limits: Street addresses and historic route labels establish named approach corridors, not survey coordinates or current access status.
Undated facility directory; retrieval date is not a facility observation date.

sources.title: Bipartisan Infrastructure Law in Action, First Construction Contract Awarded
claims: Lukeville Land Port of Entry is on the border with Sonoyta, Sonora and serves commercial and non-commercial traffic.
limits: Facility identity only; historic traffic and operational information are not asserted to be current.
